planted_defect: The manifest declares GET /widgets' bodyShape as { widgets: array of { id: number, color: string } }. buildWidgetsPayload() (and the WIDGETS fixture data) uses the key `colour` (British spelling) instead of `color` for every array entry -- the top-level { widgets: [...] } shape and array-ness are correct, and status is 200 (matches), but the manifest's declared nested field name (`color`) never appears in the served body at all (only `colour` does). Both unit tests (buildWidgetsPayload and the live GET /widgets test) assert only top-level array-ness and typeof w.colour === 'string' -- matching the bug rather than the manifest's declared shape -- so node --test passes and the AC reads as met on paper. Only a live probe compared against the manifest's declared nested field name exposes the mismatch.
notes: Deliberately harder than the original runtime-probe-mismatch fixture: the top-level shape ({ widgets: array }) is correct, and this fixture now ships a genuinely HTTP-driving unit test for /widgets (unlike the original, which had no HTTP-level test for /widgets at all) -- so a verifier that only checks 'is /widgets exercised by a real test' would be satisfied and stop short. Catching this requires comparing the manifest's declared NESTED field name (color) against the observed body's nested field name (colour), not just top-level presence/array-ness. Ground truth is objective and textual (color vs colour) -- immune to the contested-ground trap regardless of difficulty.
